diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Israel sent a message to Hezbollah and the Islamic Republic after destroying tunnels in the Ali Taher heights, warning that any response would be met with a large-scale explosion. The Israeli army has increased its alert level, especially in the air force. The 36th Division has begun redeployment and left the Ali Taher heights.
The audio version of program 24 with Fardad Farahzad has been released. The program discusses new concerns about Iran's nuclear activities deep in Kuh-e Kalang. This issue is examined in the program.

Government officials in Golestan province prevented the birthday ceremony of Shahram Baghian in Gorgan. His family members were summoned and threatened. A commitment was obtained from the family not to hold the ceremony.

Ismail Kartal resigned as Fenerbahce's head coach after a 1-1 draw against Roma in the first week of the Champions League. He made this decision together with the coaching staff to open the way for the club. Kartal thanked supporters in a press conference and stated he will not return.

The Israeli Prime Minister announced the completion of the operation to destroy Hezbollah's tunnels and underground infrastructure in the Al-Taher mountain range. The Israeli army destroyed a network of underground paths over two kilometers long. These infrastructures were built over two decades with support from the Islamic Republic.

The Israeli army announced that Hezbollah tunnels under the Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon were destroyed with over 1100 tons of explosives. Weapons and equipment made by the Islamic Republic were found in these tunnels. These tunnels served as the command center for Hezbollah's Badr regional unit.

The Wall Street Journal, citing American officials, reported that the Islamic Republic has resumed production of ballistic missiles in underground facilities using stored parts. According to the newspaper, despite heavy attacks on missile sites and industrial facilities in the first phase of the war, the assembly of liquid-fueled ballistic missiles has resumed.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported several projectiles hitting two vessels near the coast of Oman. One vessel caught fire, and the status of the second vessel is unknown. Omani authorities are investigating the incident.

Benjamin Netanyahu posted a video claiming the destruction of the Ali al-Taher tunnels in Lebanon, described as Iran's largest base abroad. The Israeli military announced it had demolished the Hezbollah tunnel network using over 1,100 tons of explosives. The military said dozens of missiles, rockets, drones, small arms, anti-tank missiles, hundreds of mines, and large quantities of explosives were discovered in the tunnels.

The audio version of Fereydoun has been released, addressing the global leftist dispute over Iranian prisoners. This audio version covers sources from The Guardian to Press TV. The main topic is the discussion of Iranian prisoners.

Alireza Kiani criticized leftist academics' stance on Iran in the program "Fereydoun." He said they claim to support the rights of the oppressed but only see the Iranian people as oppressed when it aligns with their ideological tendencies.

Jennifer Lokta, the US Deputy Representative to the UN, accused China and Russia of disrupting the enforcement of Security Council restrictions to support the Islamic Republic. She stated that the Islamic Republic continues to violate its commitments under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and IAEA safeguards agreements. The recent IAEA report confirmed this issue again.

Alireza Kiani stated on the program "Fereydoun" that Susan Abulhawa, a Palestinian-American writer, praises the Islamic Republic as the last stronghold of anti-imperialist resistance. He added that the PEN America association considers the Islamic Republic the largest prison for female writers in the world.

Anthropic company announced that Iranian government agents used the AI model 'Claude' to monitor social media content inside Iran and identify potential opponents. The company also reported identifying nine intrusion operations linked to Iran, Russia, and Turkey. Most AI-generated content in these operations received little interaction.

The Israeli ambassador to the US said the war will end when the Islamic Republic no longer exists. He emphasized that regime change in Iran is not possible without the participation of the people. Israel and the US will also play a role in this process.

Negin from Hamedan reported that during the Mahsa movement, a Sepahi kicked a 13-year-old girl in the stomach in front of her eyes. After this incident, she removed her hijab. This report was aired in a program from Iran International.

Reuters reported that attacks by the Islamic Republic damaged several US military aircraft at the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan. Donald Trump denied these reports, stating no damage occurred. The Jordanian army said 20 ballistic missiles were fired, most of which were intercepted, with no casualties.

CNN reported, citing five sources, that over 100 US military advisers in Saudi Arabia are providing intelligence and targeting support to the country. These forces operate within a newly established joint command, formed following signs of increased Iranian assistance to Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia. A US official stated the number of these forces is around 200.

The US Treasury Secretary announced that the Trump administration will sanction a major bank next Monday. The name of the bank and its country of operation were not disclosed. This action is part of the economic pressure campaign against the Islamic Republic.

Vladimir Putin arrived in Delhi to attend the two-day BRICS summit. Leaders from Russia, China, Iran, and India are present, with meetings planned. The Iran war and the Ukraine crisis are key topics of discussion.

Donald Trump predicted that after the US victory in the war with the Iranian government, gasoline prices would drop below two dollars per gallon. He forecasted the war would end shortly after the midterm elections. Trump emphasized that the Islamic Republic will never have nuclear weapons and preventing this is more important than the economic consequences of the war.

Agence France-Presse reported satellite images showing possible oil slicks near the Strait of Hormuz following US attacks on suspected IRGC-linked tankers. These slicks were observed about 20 kilometers off the Iranian coast and east of the Strait of Hormuz. The US military had previously announced the destruction of five tankers in the Sea of Oman.

Hang Cao, the acting head of the US Department of the Navy, told The Epoch Times that Islamic Republic forces have caused extensive damage to the US Navy support base in Bahrain, the home of the Fifth Fleet. Cao added that the damage has affected the ability to support the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln and the logistical requirements of long-term operations, and said that the carrier’s crew had nowhere to dock.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, at a Republican election rally in Dallas, called the Strait of Hormuz the 'Trump Strait' and said 'we control the Trump Strait.' He reiterated that we can never allow Iran to have nuclear weapons and it will not have them. Trump said that Iran is retreating everywhere.

Habib Ghasemi, a member of the Article 90 Commission, stated that to achieve real deterrence, enemy supply centers beyond the region must be targeted. He emphasized that important infrastructure and equipment should be threatened and punished. He also said that unpredictability is the key to success against the enemy.

Vahid Ahmadi called disarming Hezbollah an illusion and said negotiations under occupation are not a solution. He added that Hezbollah has become stronger after the recent war. Ahmadi also warned that Iran's strategic patience has limits regarding potential Israeli attacks.

Sadegh Beigdel announced that the discussion about the sanctions committee against the Islamic Republic has been reactivated. He said that US actions now have more international support. Also, the lack of agency access and Iran's nuclear capacity has increased concerns about the intent to build nuclear weapons.

The spouse of Saleh Mirhashami, a protester killed in December 2025, joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." She decorated his gravestone with a bouquet. This video was shared on social media.

Saba Safidi, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Tehran, was arrested on Thursday, 19 Shahrivar, to serve a sentence of three years and five months in prison. She was first taken to Jannatabad Prosecutor's Office and then transferred to Qarchak Varamin prison. This news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Mohammed bin Salman called Donald Trump twice, asking the US to target Yemen's Houthis, but Trump rejected the request. This news was reported by Axios citing two US officials. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

Yehiel Leiter, Israel's ambassador to the US, said the Islamic Republic must fall because otherwise it will find a way to rebuild. He added the regime is on the path to collapse. Continued economic pressure and sanctions by the Trump administration could lead to the Islamic Republic's defeat.

Katayoun Amiri Younesi, a civil lawyer, spoke about the rising public anger due to economic pressure and repression. She said this anger could turn into widespread protests with a spark. She believes this may happen sooner than expected.

Arina Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina reached the final of the US Open tennis tournament. Sabalenka defeated Jessica Pegula and Rybakina beat Coco Gauff to reach the final. They will face each other for the second time this year in the final of this competition.

Anthropic AI company has blocked three accounts linked to Iranian regime's advertising entities. These accounts used the 'Claude' model for influence campaigns and cognitive warfare. An interview with Kambiz Tavana was conducted by Iran International.

Amir Hayat-Moghadam announced that the American naval blockade will be broken soon. The Islamic Republic's armed forces are pursuing a new approach to counter the presence of Americans in the region. The armed forces' strategy has shifted towards a deterrent and offensive response.

Mehdi Sarami Far stated that artificial intelligence has helped increase the effectiveness of infiltration content and speed up the production of malicious codes in cyber operations. These tools also facilitate the identification of security vulnerabilities. Artificial intelligence has made it easier to produce fake emails and content for phishing operations.

The Supreme Mining Council on August 17, 2026, granted the Wrestling Federation exemption from obtaining technical and financial qualification certificates and mining exploration permits. This decision was made to compensate for some damages incurred by the federation during the 40-day war. The exemption is notable because the Wrestling Federation does not have an industrial or mining nature, and according to mining law, obtaining exploration permits requires technical and financial qualifications.

Parisa Kamali Ardakani, a political prisoner, was transferred to Bandar Abbas prison on the evening of Tuesday, September 8. She was previously serving her sentence in Yazd prison. This transfer was carried out without prior notice.
Israeli army forces are inspecting underground tunnels in the Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon using drones. The Israeli army has destroyed key tunnels built by Hezbollah in this area.

Rouhollah Rahimpour stated that Oman is trying to hold a meeting of the foreign ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council countries and the Islamic Republic. If held, the meeting aims to turn the Strait of Hormuz crisis into a regional and manageable issue. This meeting could prevent a direct confrontation between the Islamic Republic and the United States.

Security agencies of the Islamic Republic have increased pressure and interrogations on the families of the martyrs of the national revolution in various cities. These families have been threatened and summoned due to their digital activities and sharing related content. Some of their personal pages have also been blocked by the government.

The Israeli Prime Minister's Office and Ministry of Defense announced that the Israeli army has completely destroyed Hezbollah's underground infrastructure in the Ali al-Taher mountain range. Israel claims these infrastructures were built over two decades with funding and planning from the Islamic Republic. More details were provided by the Iran International reporter.

Hassanali Akhlaghi Amiri, a member of the Cultural Commission of the Parliament, announced that the military surprises of the Islamic Republic will continue. He referred to the new capabilities of the armed forces, including anti-destroyer and mine-laying missiles. He also said that targeting US military bases in the region sends clear messages to the enemies.

Two Renoir paintings were stolen from a museum in southern France. The thieves took four artworks but abandoned two paintings and took two others with them. This theft has renewed discussions about museum security in France.

Security forces launched a large-scale raid in areas of Isfahan on Thursday, September 9, detaining dozens of citizens. The arrests were reportedly related to dress code and hijab. One citizen narrated the attacks in an audio message with an AI-altered voice.

The mother of Soleiman Norouzi, a protester killed in December 2025, joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." She lit her son's grave with candles. This video was shared on social media.

Esmail Abdi cited poverty, economic inequality, lack of infrastructure, crowded classes, and child labor as main reasons for children dropping out of school in 1404. He also identified privatization and commercialization of education as factors weakening Iran's education system.

Abbas Goudarzi, spokesperson for the parliament's presidium, denied a 50% increase in MPs' salaries. He stated that MPs have received the salary increase approved in the budget law like other employees, with no additional increase currently. Goudarzi also mentioned the enemy's efforts to create division between the people and officials.

Amir Mahdi Alavi, the spokesperson of the Football Federation, explained recent controversies including the clash between Khodadad Azizi and Omid Alishah, the postponement of the Persepolis match, and the status of holding matches. He stated that the federation president has declared that matches without spectators are prohibited and all games must be held with spectators. The postponement of matches was due to requests from some clubs and approved by the league organization.

Ali Shirazi, quoting Masoud Pezeshkian, stated that the continuation of the war has led to a deadlock in providing basic needs for people and paying government employees and retirees. Pezeshkian believes that prolonging the war weakens the Islamic Republic's position in negotiations with the US.

Nasir Hosseini, the Friday prayer leader of Yasuj, stated that Mojtaba Khamenei is in full health and works more than 10 hours daily. He also claimed that Mojtaba Khamenei attended the funeral ceremony of the martyred leader in Mashhad. These statements come despite no images or audio files of Mojtaba Khamenei being released since Ali Khamenei's death.

Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency, confirmed increased construction activities at the underground facilities of Mount Kolang based on satellite images. The new images also indicate extensive use of internal routes and reinforcement of tunnel entrances. These details were reported by Ahmad Samadi, a journalist from Iran International.

The Swedish Ministry of Justice stated that the Islamic Republic has conducted activities over several years that threaten Sweden's security. The Swedish security service said Iran uses criminal networks in Sweden for violent actions. These actions target governments, groups, or individuals considered threats by the Islamic Republic.

The mother of Mahdi Ranjbari joined the 'One Candle, One Name, One Memory' campaign. She said her son was wounded by three bullets in Tehranpars on January 8, 2026, and died after ten days in the hospital.

The Wrestling Federation of the Islamic Republic was exempted from providing technical and financial qualification certificates for registering exploratory areas and participating in mining auctions. The Supreme Mining Council cited war damage compensation and support for sports and cultural activities as reasons for this decision. This news was reported in an interview with Mehdi Rostampour.

Ahmad Alamolhoda announced that by the order of Mojtaba Khamenei, four individuals who died in night gatherings in Mashhad due to a car accident are recognized as martyrs and martyr files will be created for them. This action is attributed to the leader's request. It was previously reported that the driver had a vision problem.

Mohammad Hassan Aboutorabi-Fard stated that without US warmongering, the Islamic Republic would not be in its current position of power and US bases in the region would have weakened. He described US militarism as a key factor shifting the balance of power in favor of Iran and the resistance axis. He also said the strategic Strait of Hormuz is controlled by Iranian forces and that US power is fundamentally weakening.

The Consulate General of the Islamic Republic in Dubai announced that 10 Iranian fishermen detained in the UAE have been released. These fishermen left the country on a flight from Dubai to Bandar Abbas. This news was published on Friday, 20 Shahrivar.

An Israeli official warned about the potential consequences of Houthi control over the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. He stated that the strait is at its narrowest point and its situation could be worse than the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis could target passing ships with anti-tank missiles.

Israel's Defense Minister Yisrael Katz announced that after destroying Hezbollah tunnels in southern Lebanon, the army is ready to target the group in new areas. He stated that the attack operations against Hezbollah will continue. These remarks were published by Iran International.

Lotfollah Dejkam, the Friday prayer leader of Shiraz, stated that Iran's power has become global in some fields thanks to the sacrifices of martyrs and the efforts of the people. He emphasized that enemies have been defeated in the past and will be defeated again through the people's resistance. Dejkam said that continuing this path requires patience and perseverance.

Dozens of students at Birjand University who participated in the December 2025 protests have faced confrontation, summons, and expulsion. The protests began on December 3rd in South Khorasan and spread to six counties. Seba Heydarkhani has explained these protests and their suppression.

On September 9, a citizen sent a video to Iran International criticizing the rising cost of medicine. Despite some items being covered by insurance, expenses continue to increase. Due to the heart disease of the family head, this person has taken on financial responsibilities and works from home.

The Israeli Prime Minister displayed some of the weapons removed from southern Lebanon. These weapons include artillery, air defense, missiles, mines, and computer equipment. He stated that these weapons were supplied by the Islamic Republic and are now in Israeli hands.

Nima Dadgostar from Iran International referred to a report showing that Iranian institutions use the 'Claude' model for propaganda, citizen surveillance, and identifying US military targets. Part of this usage is due to the regime's technical and economic incapacity. Some institutions use 'Claude' instead of an engineering team to develop malware and surveillance tools.

Fathollah Tavassoli, a member of parliament, demanded that Ahmad Donyamali, the Minister of Sports and Youth, explain his daughter's residence and activities in the UK. Tavassoli also announced that the number of signatures for the minister's impeachment has reached 43. He accused the minister of trying to prevent the impeachment process.

Ahmad Motahari-Asl, the Friday prayer leader of Tabriz, emphasized the enforcement of chastity and hijab laws. He called for decisive action against those promoting immorality. He also urged the government to support families and the values of chastity and hijab.

Iran's security agencies have increased pressure and interrogations on the families of the missing national revolutionaries in various cities. Recently, several family members of protest victims have been summoned by phone or directly threatened. This report is based on information received by Iran International.

A citizen from Sabzevar reported that a power outage on September 10 caused his water heater to burn out. The repair costs amid economic difficulties have worsened his living conditions. He also mentioned the government's oppression and is awaiting a call from Reza Pahlavi.

Turkey's Foreign Ministry welcomed the IAEA Board of Governors' decision to close Syria's nuclear file. Turkey stated that Damascus cooperated with the agency and showed transparency regarding activities during Bashar al-Assad's period. This news was reported by Farzia Sabti.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Iranian Foreign Ministry, said Rafael Grossi has turned the International Atomic Energy Agency into a tool for political justification and war. He added that the agency's credibility as a neutral body has been damaged and it has played a role in political preparation for an illegal war. Baqaei also stated that responsibility for military attacks includes those who provide the political and legal basis for justification.

The request for retrial by Arghavan Fallahi, a prisoner sentenced to death, was rejected by the Supreme Court. Arghavan Fallahi is a political prisoner held in Evin Prison. This decision has been declared final.
Images show a large presence of military and plainclothes forces in various areas of Isfahan. Several citizens have been arrested. Streets are blocked and vehicles stopped.

Bloomberg reported that Iran's crude oil and condensate loading decreased by about 74% in August, reaching 247,000 barrels per day. Iran's oil exports remain severely limited due to the US naval blockade. Iran's crude oil reserves have reached the highest level in several months.

Israeli army radio announced that after completing the operation to destroy Hezbollah tunnels, Israeli forces have left the Ali al-Taher heights. The forces have moved to rear positions. Israel still maintains fire control over the area.

Soda Ebrahimi Shamsabadi, a 32-year-old political prisoner in Bandar Abbas prison, has been sentenced to death for corruption on earth. She was also sentenced to confiscation of all property and dismissal from public service. The charges include insulting the leadership, media activities against national security, and cooperating with hostile governments.

The Swedish Ministry of Justice stated that the Islamic Republic has conducted activities over several years that threaten the country's security. The ministry said the Islamic Republic has used criminal networks for violent actions. This information was provided in response to Iran International.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International criticizing the poor asphalt condition in Rasht Industrial City. He pointed out problems caused by the damaged street surfaces. The video was sent to Iran International.

Ali Zarei, a political prisoner and eye injury victim from the 1401 protests, announced that his death sentence has been confirmed. He emphasized his innocence and called for support from the public and human rights organizations. Zarei was previously sentenced to death on charges of corruption on earth.

Iran Telecommunication Company announced a 45% increase in the cost of calls from landlines to mobile phones starting September 10. The call cost ceiling has risen from 625 rials to 906 rials. The financial impact of this increase will be reported in periodic financial statements.

The Israeli Prime Minister announced that Israeli forces discovered and removed a large amount of weapons during an operation in the Ali Al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon. Netanyahu said these weapons had been supplied by Iran to Hezbollah for years. The Israeli army also destroyed underground and surface infrastructure in the area.

Representatives from several Middle Eastern countries at the MEID conference in Washington viewed the end of the Islamic Republic as beneficial for the region but not certain. The Islamic Republic is severely weakened, but its collapse is not imminent and may take one to three years. Iran's economic situation was assessed as dire, and about 80% of Iranians oppose the government.

The official 25th anniversary ceremony of the September 11 terrorist attacks is being held at the Pentagon with the presence of Donald Trump and victims' families. The names of 184 victims of the Pentagon attack are read during the ceremony. An Iran International reporter is covering the event from New York.
On Thursday night in Golestan province, rainfall caused flooding in some streets and alleys in the cities of Galikesh and Gonbad Kavus. This was shown in videos received by Iran International.

Hussein Kaidi, an 18-year-old young man from Andimeshk, was shot dead by government agents in front of his home on the evening of January 9, 2026. His mother stated in a video that her son posed no threat and that she will pursue the truth about his death. She emphasized that she has not buried her grief and is seeking justice.

Nasimeh Eslamzahi, a Sunni political prisoner, was sentenced to 25 years in prison by Branch 15 of Tehran Revolutionary Court. The sentence was issued on charges of assisting in the crime of rebellion. Her husband and another defendant in the case had previously been sentenced to death and the sentences were carried out.

A Houthi fighter announced the capture of the port of Al-Mokha on the Red Sea coast in western Yemen. He stated that Saleh's forces have fled and the Houthis are advancing towards the Bab al-Mandab area. These images were released on Thursday and Friday, coinciding with the Houthis' advance along Yemen's western coast.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of War, stated at the 25th anniversary commemoration of the 9/11 attacks that the US has destroyed "the world's biggest state sponsor of terrorism" in the past six months. He added that the Iranian government has supported terrorist attacks against Americans for decades, killing thousands. Hegseth emphasized that the US ensures the Islamic Republic does not acquire nuclear weapons and that economic pressure on Iran is increasing daily.

Iran International conducted an Instagram survey about the impact of the January killings and ongoing war on people's mental health. About 38,000 people participated, and 94% said their anger is triggered more quickly than in previous years. Farshad Motaghi discussed this topic in the program "Pivast."

Hassan Ameli, the Friday prayer leader of Ardabil, stated that before the US attack, Bab al-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz were open and served the global economy. He said Trump's attack closed both routes, and now Iran will determine the oil price. Ameli described this as a power greater than the atomic bomb.

Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, attended a pre-BRICS summit in New Delhi on Friday, September 20. The meeting was held before the main BRICS summit. Vladimir Putin, Cyril Ramaphosa, and Narendra Modi were also present at the session.

The CENTCOM commander traveled to Saudi Arabia to hold meetings regarding the recent Houthi advances in Yemen. The Houthis have taken control of the port city of Al-Mokha and the southwestern coastal strip of Yemen. Al Jazeera has not released further details about these meetings.

The Houthis have gained control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea coasts, and three strategic Yemeni islands after a week of advances. Yemeni government sources stated that the group has full control over the Bab al-Mandeb area and the islands of Mayun, Greater Hanis, and Lesser Hanis. The Houthi military spokesperson announced that passage through Bab al-Mandeb is safe for all ships except Saudi vessels.
A 50-year-old truck driver died in an accident while working at the Toghroljerd coal mine in Kouhbanan county.

Saleheh Akbari, a nurse and rescue instructor, was shot and killed on the evening of January 12 in Ardabil. This happened during a security forces raid to arrest her husband. Farbod Sarvandi's report covers the life of this couple and their fate during the protests.

Reza Pahlavi stated on the anniversary of 9/11 that Iranians and Americans have never been enemies and that freedom is a shared value. He identified Islamic extremism as a common enemy that has held his country hostage. He also emphasized that freedom is the foundation of America and the goal Iranians are fighting for today.
A video shows heavy vehicles in Karaj standing in a long queue to receive diesel fuel. The video was received by Iran International. The queue situation in Karaj is depicted.

Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India, met and talked with Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, on Friday, 20 Shahrivar, in Delhi. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the annual BRICS member countries summit. The topics discussed in the meeting were not disclosed.

A video has been released showing Shoja Khalilzadeh insulting several players of the Tractor team. The Football Federation's disciplinary committee last week suspended Khodadad Azizi for four months due to insults. Khalilzadeh has a history of offensive behavior towards rival teams' fans.

Pouria Bakhtiari stated that during Ebrahim Raisi's government, he was asked to teach economic topics to Raisi. These teachings were prepared as short texts for animation and cartoon production. The content was designed to be under three minutes because Raisi's mind is fleeting.

According to TankerTrackers, the total crude oil exports of Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, UAE, and Oman from the US blockade line exceeded 10 million barrels per day for the first time in two months. This increase occurred after the practical halt of the Islamabad agreement. Iran's crude oil exports remain at zero.

The US State Department's "Rewards for Justice" program announced it has set rewards of up to $10 million for information on a number of senior al-Qaeda leaders based in Iran. The program said these individuals use Iran as a safe haven for planning and executing attacks against the US and its allies. In the published poster, rewards ranging from $3 million to $10 million have been set for information on some of these individuals, and people have been asked to provide their information.

The president of the 14th government, during his visit to India, acknowledged that US pressures on Iran have reached a 'difficult and dangerous' stage. He described the world as being at one of its 'most complex junctures' and called for 'operational cooperation' among BRICS member states.

A video shows that on Friday, 20 Shahrivar, at a gathering of Iranians living in Hanover, Germany, some supporters of Palestine were also present. Police formed a line between the two groups. This event took place at the gathering site.

In the past week, 92 illegal hunters and wood traffickers were arrested. Air pollution in some cities reached very unhealthy levels, and several fires occurred in pastures and protected areas. Additionally, a decline in the Asiatic cheetah population and extensive fish deaths in the Zayandeh Rud river were reported.

Jamshid Barzegar said the September 11 attacks changed US foreign policy and global developments. Fighting terrorist groups and the Islamic Republic has become a priority for Washington. Linking the anniversary of September 11 to the current war against the Islamic Republic indicates the continuation of the counter-terrorism strategy.
Videos sent to Iran International show a large fire in the Ashkan mountains in the south of Noorabad, Mamasani on Friday, September 11.

Reza Najafi, Iran's representative to the IAEA, said the US might use the new IAEA resolution to escalate conflicts and start military operations against Iran. He called the IAEA's decision to refer Iran's case to the UN Security Council political and stated that Iran's cooperation with the agency continues. Najafi emphasized that Iran will decide its response after assessing the resolution's consequences.

An Anthropic researcher resigned due to fears about the future of artificial intelligence. He warns that a self-improving superintelligence could become a threat to human survival within this decade. He also raised questions about who should decide how and where this technology is used if even its creators are uncertain about controlling it.
The mother of Matin Montazer-ozur distributed food in memory of her killed son. Matin Montazer-ozur was 32 years old and from Gorgan. He was shot dead on January 7, 2026, in the city of Shahroud.

Daily wage workers of Bampur municipality reported non-payment of about six months' wages and non-deposit of insurance for the past year. Municipality officials have threatened workers with dismissal if they protest the situation.

A citizen posted a video showing a queue of heavy vehicles at the Chabahar cargo terminal. He says the 250-liter gasoline quota is sold for eight million tomans. Also, they have to wait in line for hours to get the quota.

Hadi Choopan, former Mr. Olympia champion, said in a video interview that he tried for 10 years to help Hani Rambod grow. He added that he never thought the day would come when Hani Rambod would be the reason for his downfall.

Two weeks before the new school year begins, officials of the Islamic Republic have commented on stricter enforcement of mandatory hijab in educational centers. Gholamali Haddad Adel said that the current war conditions prevent serious engagement with the hijab issue. This topic was evaluated by Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst.

A number of Iranians gathered on Tuesday, 17 Shahrivar, in the central square of Hamburg. They protested against inflation and executions in Iran. The protesters demanded the release of political prisoners.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated during his visit to Mount Hermon that the main task is to defeat the terrorist regime of Iran and that Israel is very close to this goal. He emphasized that Israel will not allow any terrorist army to be stationed on its borders. Netanyahu also declared that Israel controls the entire area from Mount Hermon to the Mediterranean.

The spokesperson of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the restricted area of the Islamic Republic from around Chabahar to parts of the Oman Sea and Arabian Sea. Vessels entering this area without coordination will be placed on the sanctions list. They will also be denied passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

Snapbox drivers in Semnan stopped working in protest against low fares, fuel costs, and commission rates. They announced that none of the drivers are currently working. This protest was seen in a video published on social media.

South Korea has entered a new phase of considering various options, including possible military participation against the Islamic Republic. Japan is focusing on diplomatic channels and direct talks with the Islamic Republic. These movements coincide with rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US Department of Defense is considering scenarios for rapid amphibious operations by Marines on uninhabited Iranian islands near the Strait of Hormuz. The goal is to turn these islands into surveillance and logistical bases to protect commercial ships. The USS Tripoli, with 3,500 Marines, is present in the area, and F-35B fighters will provide air support.

On Tuesday night, with increased security measures, several government motorcycle forces were deployed in the streets of Mashhad. This was shown in a video received by Iran International. The action was taken in response to security conditions.

Ali Tajernia explained that if the transfer window does not open, the two players will stay with Aluminium until mid-season and then return to Esteghlal. Esteghlal has fulfilled its financial commitments and provided the players to Aluminium without cost. He also emphasized the importance of loyalty to commitments in football.

The Hercules Star oil tanker near Dubai experienced an incident resulting in one crew member killed and another missing. The chartering company stated that a specialized team is searching for the missing crew, and other crew members are safe. Initial assessments indicate a possible drone attack on the tanker.
A video posted on social media shows a citizen visiting the Tomb of the Immortals. The person placed flowers on their gravestone. This event has been reflected in the virtual space.

The case of 18 prisoners in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan has been referred to the Revolutionary Court. They are accused of involvement in unrest and arson at the prison. They face the risk of receiving death sentences.

Mohammad Ali Ghadousi, head of the legal department of the Football Federation, stated that managers have not yet received official notification about the indictment. The case concerns a $20,000 bonus paid to board members after qualifying for the 2022 World Cup. Yashar Soltani also reported that indictments have been issued against several senior federation managers on embezzlement charges.

A citizen stated in a video that barrels containing gasoline or oil are being transported from Mahshahr refinery to Nakja Abad by trailer. This has happened recently. No further details have been provided.
A citizen reported paying 653,000 tomans for a roll of tape and a pack of labels. This was reported via a video to Iran International. The prices of these items have significantly increased.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center announced that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile 28 nautical miles southeast of Iraq's Faw port. The tanker crew are safe and no environmental consequences have been reported so far. Authorities are investigating the incident and have urged vessels to exercise caution.

A citizen sarcastically commented in a video sent to Iran International that they are happy there is no electricity and the house is dark. He added that if they are not happy, they will be executed. This statement refers to the power outage situation.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry stated that the armed forces will respond decisively to any US aggression. This statement was issued after the US attacked several Iranian oil tankers on September 7. The ministry called these attacks a violation of international law and urged the UN Security Council to take action.

The Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned the recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia. Ankara warned about the threat to civilians and called for an immediate halt to the Houthis' aggressive actions. These attacks have escalated regional tensions and undermined diplomatic efforts to end the conflict in Yemen.

Two citizens commemorated the memory of the deceased in the December 2025 protests by lighting candles for Masoud Zatparvar and Esmail Beigi Harchgani. This was done by sending videos to Iran International. These individuals are recognized as martyrs.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, head coach of Esteghlal, stated before the match against Paykan that his team aims to win three points. He mentioned the players' fatigue due to recent travels and the need to manage their energy. He also commented on the attack line and the presence of players in the youth team.

Ebrahim Rezaei stated that Iran's membership in the NPT treaty has brought no benefit and sensitive information has been exposed to espionage. He criticized the IAEA for not aiding Iran's nuclear technology and called its director a Western agent. The Islamic Republic will respond to any possible IAEA Board of Governors resolution.

A member of Iran International's editorial team referred to the Pakistani defense minister's remarks about the possible activation of the Makkah defense pact. He said the military readiness of Turkey and Pakistan to defend Saudi Arabia and the global reactions against the Houthis indicate a major decision to close the proxy conflict in Yemen.

The official funeral ceremony of Harald V, the former king of Norway, was held today in Oslo. Members of royal families and high-ranking officials from various countries attended the ceremony. Tens of thousands are expected to be present along the procession route and in central Oslo.

A member of Iran International's editorial team referred to Pakistan's defense minister's remarks about the possible activation of the Makkah defense pact. Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are ready to support Riyadh in the war against the Houthis if the current situation in the region continues. Additionally, the recapture of Sanaa and securing the Bab al-Mandab Strait have become priorities.

Aban and Hassan Mousavi, siblings arrested in connection with the December 2025 protests, are spending their 200th day in temporary detention at Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. They face charges of moharebeh and remain in judicial uncertainty. So far, temporary release on bail has not been granted to them.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported an attack on a vessel 24 miles northwest of Rashid Port, Dubai. The tanker captain observed the vessel leaning, possibly due to water ingress after an unknown projectile hit. Authorities are investigating and have urged vessels to exercise caution and report suspicious activity.

Gholamali Haddad Adel stated that due to wartime conditions, the government cannot fully address the issue of hijab at the moment. He added that the influence of promoting Western lifestyle in schools is evident. He also mentioned that dealing with this issue is now more difficult than in the 1980s.

Jane Lawson has launched the "Golestan" project to create a global reference for Iranian performing arts from 1880 to 1980. This digital archive includes solo performances, plays, radio programs, and other related works. The materials are indexed and searchable by relevant keywords.
Videos sent by citizens to Iran International show a missile passing over the skies of Abhar and Khomein in the early morning of September 8.

Brent crude oil price reached 100 dollars per barrel for the first time since early August. This price increase occurred amid ongoing conflicts in the Persian Gulf. The US announced it destroyed five oil tankers linked to the Revolutionary Guard after unsuccessful missile attacks by Iran.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, addressed the US Secretary of Defense on September 8 via a Telegram post. He stated that the next target is the US energy assets in the region. This message was shared on social media.

The Islamic Republic launched a missile attack on Jordan. This attack has increased concerns about the expansion of conflict in the region. Tehran's target was a base used by American forces in Jordan.

Citizens reported the simultaneous passage of several missiles over the skies of Shahin Shahr, Najafabad, Khomeinishahr, and Baharestan. The number of missiles was reported to be between 4 and 9. The launch sites were identified as two military bases in Najafabad.

Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open quarterfinals to advance to the semifinals. The five-set match ended with scores of 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, and 7-6 in favor of Shelton. Shelton will face Frances Tiafoe in the semifinals.

Pakistan has expressed its support for Saudi Arabia's right to defend its territory and citizens. The Pakistani Ministry of Foreign Affairs considers this right legitimate. This statement continues Pakistan's regional support for Saudi Arabia against proxy attacks by the Islamic Republic.

Ahmad Alavi, an economist, reported the intensification of the drug and treatment crisis in Iran. He identified the insurance budget deficit as a cause of the government's financial crisis and resource allocation issues. Financial pressure on pharmacies has led to direct treatment costs being passed to patients and the expansion of the drug black market.

Ruhollah Rahimpour stated that the CENTCOM strategic operation indicates the US is seeking to increase economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. He added that targeting Iranian oil tankers could directly pressure Iran's oil exports and foreign currency revenues.

Lionel Messi has reached a preliminary agreement with the owners of the Spanish club Eldense to purchase the team. Eldense recently promoted to La Liga 2, and Messi intends to acquire 100% of its shares without third-party involvement. Finalizing the deal requires approval from the Spanish High Sports Council.

A citizen in a video shared on social media criticized the economic and social situation and expressed concern about the future of children in Iran. He addressed those responsible for the current situation, saying they have suffered and are worried about the children's future. This video has gained attention on social media.

A birthday ceremony for Fathollah Avari was held at his gravesite. Fathollah Avari was one of the detainees from December 2025 who was executed on June 3, 2026. This news is based on a video received by Iran International.

Kamran Ghazanfari, a Tehran representative, said we are practically on the brink of World War III due to international tensions. He assessed the likelihood of the US using nuclear weapons against Iran as very low. He also mentioned that the plan for Iran to exit the NPT treaty might be reconsidered in parliament.

An audio file reveals that a US military aircraft warned three Iranian oil tankers that their engine rooms would be targeted for violating a military blockade. The crew was asked to leave the engine rooms within 10 minutes. US forces targeted five oil tankers linked to the IRGC.

Raf Chikoni, head of the Australian parliamentary security committee, condemned the threats by the Islamic Republic's armed forces spokesperson against Persian-language media. He emphasized the right of journalists to work freely. Expelling the Iranian ambassador and sanctioning government agents were mentioned as possible Australian responses.

People from various cities in Iran have reported economic problems and drug shortages. Medical and pharmaceutical costs have increased, and some vital medicines are unavailable. There are also significant increases in prices and living expenses, especially electricity bills and car repairs.

The US, UK, France, and Germany submitted a draft resolution against the Islamic Republic to the IAEA Board of Governors. The resolution calls for referring Iran's nuclear case to the UN Security Council. This action is due to Tehran's failure to comply with nuclear non-proliferation commitments.

The Washington Post reported that Persian Gulf countries are strengthening their defense capabilities and creating alternative routes to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing US-Iran war. Officials from the UAE and Qatar have stated that reliance on US security support is insufficient and regional countries must build more independent defense capabilities.

Abdolhossein Khosropanah, Secretary of the Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution, stated that there is a lack of hijab observance in some government offices and pharmacies. He emphasized that all executive bodies are required to monitor compliance with hijab regulations. He also mentioned that the council does not see a need for new regulations on chastity and hijab.

The US has sanctioned 27 Iranian airlines and foreign companies linked to Mahan Air. These sanctions target the transfer of personnel, sensitive equipment, and financial resources of the Islamic Republic. Additionally, the suspension of aviation licenses and maritime pressures create new restrictions on Tehran's external communications.

Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, described the Houthis as Iran's proxy forces and stated that Washington is closely monitoring the group's activities and the Islamic Republic's role in regional affairs.

Esmail Baghai, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that the Strait of Hormuz is under full control of the Islamic Republic's armed forces. He mentioned that after the Islamabad agreement, the security situation improved but the US violated the agreement. Additionally, negotiations between the Islamic Republic and Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz are ongoing.

Alireza Salimi, a member of the parliament's presidium, stated that the way to confront Israel is through resistance and a strong response. He criticized the Lebanese government's approach towards Israel, calling it a black mark on its political record. Salimi also emphasized that the Islamic Republic has always supported the resistance and will continue to do so.

Sadegh Beigdeli stated that the sanctions on 27 Iranian airlines and the network related to Mahan Air make the transfer of sensitive equipment, financial resources, and personnel by the Islamic Republic more difficult and costly. He added that simultaneous pressure on air and sea routes forces Tehran to use land routes more extensively. These routes are slower, more expensive, and have limited capacity.

Erfan Ghaneifard, a Middle East analyst, told Iran International that US intelligence and security cooperation with regional countries has entered a broad phase. He also believes that the expansion of the war by Tehran could lead to the formation of a regional coalition against the Islamic Republic.

The US Treasury Department announced that the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has sanctioned 27 Iranian airlines and seven aviation-related companies. Among the sanctioned entities are Ata, Chabahar, Iran Airtour, Aseman, Kish, Karun, Qeshm, Sepehran, Taban, Zagros, Varesh, and Fly Persia.

Mohammad Saleh Jokar warned that if the US continues the naval blockade, it will face a devastating response. He stated that US missile systems can no longer track Iranian missiles. Additionally, Iran's military and missile capabilities have significantly improved compared to the past.

Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old researcher at Anthropic, is leaving the AI industry due to concerns about competition among tech companies to develop self-improving AI models. He warned that competition between American and Chinese companies could lead to compromises in safety. Over a thousand AI researchers have called for global coordination to slow down the development of self-improving models.

The family of Niloufar Majavari, who died last week following torture and assault, gathered at her grave in Zargatan Cemetery, Piranshahr, to condemn her murder. The suspect is still at large, and police and judiciary are investigating the injuries and working to arrest him. After Niloufar was declared brain dead, her family agreed to donate her two kidneys.

The price of gasoline outside the quota in Iran has increased to 100,000 rials per liter. This increase can generate less than 500 million dollars in additional annual revenue for the government. However, it will have limited impact on the fuel shortage.

The US, UK, France, and Germany have prepared a draft resolution to refer Iran's nuclear case to the UN Security Council. The draft has not yet been formally submitted to the IAEA Board of Governors, and negotiations are ongoing. The IAEA has warned that lack of inspector access to Iran's nuclear sites poses a proliferation risk that must be urgently addressed.

Oil prices have risen for the fourth consecutive day, nearing $100 per barrel. This increase followed the US announcement of destroying five oil tankers linked to the IRGC and a missile attack by the IRGC on a US base in Jordan. Analysts have suggested the possibility of Brent oil prices surging above $120.

Raf Chikoni, head of the Australian Parliament's intelligence committee, called the threats against Persian-speaking journalists by the IRGC unacceptable and emphasized their right to work freely. He urged global support for the Iranian people and the Iranian diaspora. Chikoni mentioned actions such as expelling Iranian diplomats and sanctioning individuals linked to the IRGC in Australia.

Richard Goldberg, an analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, wrote that the IRGC is in a losing position in its policy of escalating tensions. He added that each attack accelerates the organization's collapse. Additionally, the IRGC's tanker and air fleets are at risk of destruction and grounding.

Ellen Burstyn, a 93-year-old American actress, received the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at the 83rd Venice Film Festival. In her speech, she highlighted the changing role of women in cinema and expressed hope for greater female presence. Report by Sadaf Baghbani, Iran International reporter.

Chuck Schumer, the Democratic minority leader in the US Senate, accused Donald Trump of dragging the US into an endless war. He said this war has caused soaring prices and endangered military forces abroad. Schumer emphasized that the war must end immediately.

Amir Mobarez Parasta stated that multiple networks in mental health and treatment have been established abroad to support families seeking justice. These supports can be provided through medical staff inside Iran and specialized networks abroad. The main goal is to ensure these families do not feel alone.

The price of some medicines in Iran has increased up to five times in one year. Patients' out-of-pocket expenses have reached about 80 percent. This situation has forced patients to make difficult choices.

Jamshid Barzegar said the increase in gasoline prices not only raises fuel costs but also leads to higher prices for goods and services and economic pressure on people. He added that the Islamic Republic has no plan to compensate for the gasoline deficit. Concerns about widespread protests have prevented further gasoline price increases.

The company Tanker Trackers reported that five Iranian oil tankers targeted by the US military on Tuesday have exported a total of 45 million barrels of crude oil and petroleum products since May 2019.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi stated that the goal of the Islamic Republic's attacks on American ships is to break sanctions and increase pressure on the Trump administration. These actions aim to force the US to withdraw from the region. Tensions in the area have escalated following these attacks.

Yemeni government forces have taken control of the Al-Atmah area in Al-Jawf province. A large-scale operation has started in Al-Bayda province, and clashes continue in the western coast and west of Taiz. After repelling recent Houthi ground attacks, government forces have launched a counterattack.
The US Central Command destroyed five oil tankers carrying Iranian crude oil. This action followed missile attacks by the IRGC on a US warship. No American personnel were harmed in these attacks.

The US Central Command announced that American forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday. This action followed two attempts by the IRGC to target a US warship. CENTCOM identified the tankers as part of a network financing the IRGC.

Recent reports have emerged about the theft of food items such as cheese, yogurt, cream, rice, and oil. Some accused individuals have no prior criminal record and have been arrested for theft for the first time. This issue raises concerns about the economic and living conditions of the people.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, stated that if Iran attempts to attack US Navy ships, Iranian oil tankers will be targeted. This statement reflects ongoing tensions between the two countries. Rubio directly threatened a retaliatory response.
